q: What do these two pedestrian signals mean?
a: White walking person: pedestrians may cross. Orange hand: pedestrians must not begin to cross
w: Walking person: cars may go. Hand: cars must stop
Walking person: school zone. Hand: crossing guard ahead
e: Walk = white walking symbol. Don't start = flashing or steady orange hand.
s: The signal for pedestrians to walk is a white walking symbol. A flashing or steady orange hand symbol means pedestrians must not begin to cross.

q: What do yellow lines and white lines on the road tell you?
a: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions; white lines separate traffic going the same direction
w: Yellow lines are for passing; white lines are for no passing
Yellow lines mark bike lanes; white lines mark car lanes
Yellow lines are temporary; white lines are permanent
e: Yellow = opposite directions. White = same direction.
s: Yellow lines separate traffic travelling in opposite directions. White lines separate traffic travelling in the same direction.

q: What does a white arrow painted on your lane mean?
a: You may move only in the direction of the arrow
w: It's a suggestion for the best route
e: Lane arrows are rules: follow the arrow.
s: A white arrow painted on a lane means you may move only in the direction of the arrow.

q: Which picture shows a stop line?
a: markings/3-5.jpg
e: A stop line is a single white line across the road where you must stop.
s: A stop line is a single white line painted across the road at an intersection. It shows where you must stop.

q: Which picture shows a crosswalk marked by two parallel white lines?
a: markings/3-6.jpg
e: Two parallel white lines across the road = crosswalk.
s: A crosswalk is marked by two parallel white lines painted across the road.

q: Which picture shows a pedestrian crossover (double white lines with an X in each approaching lane)?
a: markings/2-23.jpg
e: Crossovers have signs, overhead yellow lights, double white lines and an X in each lane approaching them.
s: Pedestrian crossovers are marked by two white double parallel lines across the road with an X in each lane approaching it.

q: Which picture shows continuity lines (wider, closer-together broken lines)?
a: markings/3-4.jpg
e: Continuity lines mark lanes that are ending or exiting, like at on-ramps and off-ramps.
s: Broken lines that are wider and closer together than regular broken lines are called continuity lines.

q: There is a solid line on the left of your lane. What does it mean?
a: It is unsafe to pass
w: You may pass if the way is clear
e: Solid = don't pass. Broken = you may pass if it's clear.
s: A solid line at the left of your lane means it is unsafe to pass.

q: There is a broken line on the left of your lane. What does it mean?
a: You may pass if the way is clear and there's enough room ahead to finish the pass
e: A broken line allows passing, but only when it's safe.
s: A broken line at the left of your lane means you may pass if the way is clear.

q: You see continuity lines (wide, close-together broken lines) on your LEFT side. What does it usually mean?
a: Your lane is ending or exiting; change lanes if you want to keep going the same way
w: You may pass on the left
e: Continuity lines on your left = your lane ends or exits. On your right = your lane continues.
s: When you see continuity lines on your left side, it generally means the lane you are in is ending or exiting and that you must change lanes if you want to continue in your current direction.

q: The continuity lines are on your RIGHT side. What does that mean?
a: Your lane will continue unaffected
e: Right side = your lane continues. Left side = your lane is ending or exiting.
s: Continuity lines on your right mean your lane will continue unaffected.

q: Crosswalk vs stop line: what marks a crosswalk?
a: Two parallel white lines across the road
w: A single white line across the road
Double white lines with an X before them
e: Stop line = one white line. Crosswalk = two parallel lines. Crossover = double lines with an X.
s: A crosswalk is marked by two parallel white lines painted across the road.

q: Two solid lines guide traffic around a bridge pier, and the pier is painted yellow and black. What do these markings mean?
a: They guide traffic away from a fixed object and warn you about it
e: Solid lines lead you around the object, and the yellow and black paint warns you it's there.
s: Two solid lines painted on the pavement guide traffic away from fixed objects such as bridge piers or concrete islands.

q: A pedestrian started crossing on the walk signal, and now the orange hand appears. Who has the right-of-way?
a: The pedestrian, until they finish crossing
w: The cars, as soon as the hand appears
The cars, if they have a green light
e: Pedestrians already crossing should hurry, but they still have the right-of-way.
s: While they are crossing, pedestrians still have the right-of-way over vehicles.

q: What colour is the hand symbol that tells pedestrians not to start crossing?
a: Orange
e: Walk = white walking person. Don't start = orange hand (flashing or steady).
s: A flashing or steady orange hand symbol means pedestrians must not begin to cross.

q: Which lines separate traffic travelling in opposite directions?
a: Yellow lines
e: Yellow = opposite directions. White = same direction.
s: Yellow lines separate traffic travelling in opposite directions.

q: What does a stop line look like?
a: A single white line painted across the road
w: A yellow line across the road
A white X in the lane
e: One white line = stop line. Two lines = crosswalk.
s: A stop line is a single white line painted across the road at an intersection.

q: Besides signs and overhead yellow lights, how is a pedestrian crossover marked on the road?
a: Two white double parallel lines across the road, with an X in each approaching lane
e: Look for the X on the road before the crossing.
s: Pedestrian crossovers are identified by specific signs, overhead yellow lights, and pavement markings.

q: Pedestrians are using this crossover. When may you go?
a: Only after they have completely crossed the road and cleared the roadway
w: As soon as they've passed your lane
When they reach the middle of the road
Right away, if you honk first
e: At a crossover, wait until pedestrians are all the way across.
s: Drivers and cyclists must stop before the line and yield to pedestrians until pedestrians have completely crossed the road and cleared the roadway.

q: There's no stop line, no crosswalk and no sidewalk. Where do you stop for a red light?
a: At the edge of the intersection
w: In the middle of the intersection
One car length past the light
e: Stop line, then crosswalk, then edge of the sidewalk, then edge of the intersection.
s: If there is no sidewalk, stop at the edge of the intersection.

q: There's no stop line, but there is a crosswalk. Where do you stop?
a: At the crosswalk (marked or not)
w: At the far side of the intersection
At the edge of the intersection
e: No stop line? Stop at the crosswalk.
s: If there is no stop line marked on the road, stop at the crosswalk, marked or not.

q: You're on a two-lane road with a broken yellow line on your left. A slow vehicle is ahead, and the road ahead is clear. What may you do?
a: Pass, if there are enough broken lines ahead to finish the pass safely
w: Never pass on a two-lane road
Pass only if the driver waves you on
e: Broken line = passing allowed when it's clear and you have room to finish.
s: ('A' may pass if there are enough broken lines ahead to complete the pass safely.)

q: You're behind a slow truck and there's a solid line on your left. What should you do?
a: Stay behind it: it's unsafe to pass
w: Pass if the truck driver waves you on
e: A solid line on your left means don't pass.
s: A solid line at the left of your lane means it is unsafe to pass.

q: Your lane has a white arrow pointing only left. What must you do at the intersection?
a: Turn left
w: You may do anything if no one is behind you
e: White lane arrows: you may move only in the direction of the arrow.
s: A white arrow painted on a lane means you may move only in the direction of the arrow.

q: Can pedestrians cross on a left-turn green arrow?
a: No, not unless a pedestrian signal tells them to
w: Yes, if no cars are turning
e: Pedestrians may not cross on a flashing green light or a left-turn green arrow.
s: Pedestrians may not cross on a flashing green light or a left-turn green arrow.
